title: Partition of Bengal is implemented
detail: British authorities divided Bengal, triggering immediate political resistance, boycott campaigns, and debates over identity and representation.

title: Sustained anti-partition mobilization grows
detail: Political leaders, civic groups, and sections of the public maintained prolonged protest and organizational pressure against the partition arrangement.

title: Partition of Bengal is annulled
detail: At the Delhi Durbar, the British Crown announced the reversal of the 1905 partition and the reunification of Bengal.

title: Imperial capital shifts from Calcutta to Delhi
detail: Alongside annulment, the colonial state moved the capital, signaling a wider administrative recalibration beyond Bengal alone.

title: Legacy shapes later Bengal and subcontinental politics
detail: Although partition was reversed, the episode left lasting effects on political alignments, constitutional debates, and communal dynamics.
